title: Receipt Rage Confession Booth
oneLiner: A shareable consumer vent booth that turns hidden fees and terrible service stories into a clean complaint poster and action script.

sourceSignals.signal: Customer complaints are rising as consumers feel trapped by fees, poor service, monopolies, and dynamic pricing.
Major retailers are rolling out digital shelf tags, sparking fear that faster updates could become dynamic or discriminatory pricing.
Michigan legislators are moving to ban surveillance pricing while many states consider similar algorithmic pricing rules.

stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web prototype for "Receipt Rage Confession Booth", a shareable consumer vent booth that turns hidden fees and terrible service stories into a clean complaint poster and action script. Target user: consumers angry about fees, dynamic prices, and service dead-ends who want to vent without sounding chaotic. Build the key UX around entering a fee/service story, classifying the rage type, generating a poster, and receiving a practical complaint script or policy action link. Required UI sections: rage story intake, hidden fee autopsy, complaint tone selector, shareable poster generator, and action script and escalation links. Design direction: use the premium-editorial profile with refined contrast, editorial typography, one quiet CTA color, and polished complaint-card layouts. Use source signals S15, S1, and S3 as problem evidence only.
